A1.justification: Both complete 30-page PDFs describe the same SDDS research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison; the appendix pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original combinatorial-optimization experiments, Ising observable estimates, ablations, and Edwards-Anderson experiments in Section 5 and Appendices A.7–A.8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–4, the appendix experiments, and Figure 1.

M1.justification: The forward-KL and reverse-KL training methods, diffusion-based SN-NIS/NMCMC procedures, architectures, and algorithms remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A.3–A.4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same graph-optimization benchmarks, RB-100 ablation, 24×24 Ising model, and Edwards-Anderson sampling and ground-state scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main and appendix tables, including DiffUCO, LTFT, Gurobi, autoregressive baselines, and the CQO/VQA/RVQA/VNA comparisons.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, sample counts, computational budgets, diffusion-step settings, and testing procedures are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices A.7–A.10.

E4.justification: The learning-rate/GraphNorm ablation in Table 6 and diffusion-step, memory, and runtime analyses in Figure 1 and Table 7 are identical. No additional ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Seed counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are retained, including the three training seeds in Table 1 and three independent sampling runs in Appendix A.7.3.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains the fKL free-energy estimate of -2.11209 ± 0.00008.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, objectives, sampling derivations, and policy-gradient proofs remain unchanged. The new script reference adds no mathematical result or correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about memory-efficient diffusion training, state-of-the-art UCO results, and unbiased-sampling advantages over autoregressive approaches.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the mass-covering versus mode-seeking interpretation, DiffUCO's Ising failure discussion, hardware-comparison caveat, and coverage-related sampling limitations.

D1.justification: v1 provides a general repository link; v3 adds footnote 1 in Section 5.2 linking specifically to IsingTheory.py for computing finite-size Ising observables. This adds code-access guidance without establishing any change to the implementation or experiments.

R1.justification: Related work, research positioning, and bibliography are unchanged. Ferdinand and Fisher (1969), beside which the new script footnote appears, was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short explanatory script footnote and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The title changes from two lines with a split word to three lines without that split. The added footnote causes local reflow on pages 9–11; figure and table designs, captions, and contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The specific Ising-observable script reference in Section 5.2 improves reproducibility guidance beyond v1's general repository link by identifying where readers can find the reference calculation. This is a limited documentation benefit; the scientific methods, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
